input.brief: Which of our four growth bets should get next quarter budget?

candidates.label: served_v17
candidates.note: Verbatim decision_review object extracted from the arm's raw model text (json_text).

output.narrative_summary: This result rests on how Customer Acquisition Cost feeds through to New Revenue. If that cost rises enough, more runs could support a different option. In this model, 41% of runs supported Self Serve Funnel.

story_headlines.opt_selfserve: Self Serve Funnel holds up because its modelled outcome stays strong even as acquisition cost varies.
story_headlines.opt_paid: Paid Acquisition would need acquisition cost to fall for more runs to support it.
story_headlines.opt_partner: Partner Channel would need a stronger modelled revenue outcome relative to its acquisition cost to gain runs.
story_headlines.opt_outbound: Outbound Sales would need its modelled outcome range to narrow and lift for more runs to support it.

robustness_explanation.summary: The ordering holds in about 64% of variations, a moderate level based on current estimates.
robustness_explanation.primary_risk: The link from Customer Acquisition Cost to New Revenue is the main point of fragility in this result.
stability_factors: Self Serve Funnel keeps a favourable modelled outcome range across most variations tested.
fragility_factors: The link from Customer Acquisition Cost to New Revenue could flip which option more runs support.

output.readiness_rationale: The comparison is settled enough to act on, though Customer Acquisition Cost is the one factor worth confirming before committing budget.

fac_cac.specific_action: Pull actual blended acquisition cost from the last full quarter of spend data rather than relying on the modelled estimate.
fac_cac.rationale: This factor has the highest value evidence you could gather for this decision.
fac_cac.decision_hygiene: Estimate the current acquisition cost yourself before looking at the actual figure.

edge_cac_growth.trigger_description: If Customer Acquisition Cost rises well beyond current levels...
edge_cac_growth.consequence: ...then the most runs would support Paid Acquisition rather than Self Serve Funnel.

flip_thresholds.narrative: If Customer Acquisition Cost moves from 420 GBP to 610 GBP, more runs would support a different option.

key_assumptions: The link from Customer Acquisition Cost to New Revenue assumes current market conditions hold.
The brief frames this as a single quarter's budget choice among four distinct growth bets.

decision_quality_prompts.question: This failed because Customer Acquisition Cost rose sharply after budget was committed to Self Serve Funnel, what would that look like in hindsight?
decision_quality_prompts.applies_because: The comparison is settled enough to act on, but the result rests on a factor with real room to move.

pre_mortem.failure_scenario: Self Serve Funnel was funded, but Customer Acquisition Cost rose well beyond the modelled level and eroded the expected New Revenue advantage.
warning_signs: Acquisition cost trending upward quarter over quarter
New Revenue growth falling short of the modelled range
pre_mortem.mitigation: Track acquisition cost against the modelled level monthly and reassess if it drifts upward.
pre_mortem.review_trigger: Reconvene if acquisition cost moves materially before the next planning cycle
